linux_clean_clone_differences: application package hashes were computed in filesystem read order, so a hash pinned on APFS could not validate on ext4. This is R2-D5. The canonical baseline had passed the same job on Linux only because readdir order happened to agree, which made the gate a coin flip on every runner rather than a platform-specific failure. Repaired by ordering the walk; the pinned hashes were already the sorted-order hashes, so no package or evidence was regenerated.
tests/test_m121_app_runtime.py and tests/test_m87_knowledge_grounding.py were not in the bounded local suite, so neither failure could be seen before publication. Both files are now in it.

tests/test_m17_computer_agent.py::test_replay_redacts_credentials is a pre-existing time-dependent flake. It asserts the replay blob contains neither the password 'hunter2' nor the OTP '999'. Both are redacted correctly and always were — proven by holding time.time() fixed — but the blob also carries two raw time.time() floats, and the assertion fails whenever a timestamp's decimal expansion happens to contain the substring '999'. Measured at about 0.37 percent per timestamp, so roughly 0.7 percent per run. The redaction control never failed; the test's own oracle is unsound. Not a convergence regression and not touched by R2, so it was recorded rather than repaired, and the job was re-run to obtain an authoritative result. It is a genuine defect and belongs to whichever program owns that suite.

tests/test_m17_1_live.py::test_live_browser_launch_and_close and ::test_live_browser_dom_and_click failed on the canonical baseline's Linux run and passed on both trunk-v3 runs. Pre-existing contention-sensitive flake, not touched by R2, recorded rather than claimed as a fix.

notes: R2 converged three independently-advanced program heads — UI-NEXT through 3.1 with T-NEXT through 4 as the base, V-NEXT through 2B.6 merged onto it, and the M64 route repair plus the two R1 recovery commits cherry-picked — onto one trunk. R1 was cherry-picked rather than merged because its branch sits on the condensed voice line, which would have contested V-NEXT's ownership of the voice runtime. The V-NEXT merge produced exactly two textual conflicts, resolved COMBINE and ADAPT and recorded in the manifest. Convergence exposed four real defects that no single input line could have surfaced alone; all four are repaired in this trunk. Certification was rebuilt so it cannot lie about what it tested: frontend and backend each report their SHA and worktree at runtime, the certificate records both, and the run fails closed if they disagree or if a foreign backend origin is observed. At this SHA the trunk is integrated, locally tested, and browser-certified, and it is neither published nor CI-verified nor merged. Those are three distinct unmet conditions and none of them may be reported as completion.
